claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component conditions.
Atomic-scale lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr creates a fine, heterogeneous microstructure.
The distortion-induced heterogeneous microstructure activates additional slip systems and enhances dislocation mobility.
The distortion-induced microstructure promotes dynamic recovery.
Additional slip activity, enhanced dislocation mobility, and dynamic recovery delay crack initiation and propagation.
The initial WTaTiVZr material is polycrystalline and multiphase.
Identically processed WTaTiVZr and commercially pure tungsten specimens will be compared using the same high-temperature strain rates and thermal-cycling protocols.
Sub-grain refinement, nanoscale precipitates, or elemental segregation constitute the microstructural heterogeneity caused by lattice distortion.
Atomic misfit among W, Ta, Ti, V, and Zr creates localized stress concentrations that lower the effective Peierls barrier.
Lowering the effective Peierls barrier activates more slip systems and encourages dynamic recovery in WTaTiVZr.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit higher dislocation density than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit more active slip systems and finer sub-grains than pure tungsten.
Commercially pure tungsten has a high ductile-to-brittle transition and limited slip-system activation, leading to lower plastic strain and toughness.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply primarily at high temperatures where dislocation movement and multiple slip systems are activated.
The mechanism may not apply at low temperatures or when irradiation-induced phase transformations dominate deformation.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase in both plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to observe increased dislocation activity, additional slip-system activation, or sub-grain refinement associated with lattice distortion would falsify the proposed mechanism.
